chains.summary: The mind is restless, strong, and stubborn, as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees that by practice and letting go it is held. Little by little, with understanding held firm, the mind is brought back each time it wanders. To the one whose mind is calm, the highest happiness comes.
chains.title: The mind is hard to hold, and can be trained

verses.m: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥

verses.m: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verses.sa: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥

verses.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥

chains.summary: Pleasures born of contact are wombs of sorrow. They begin and end. The wise do not delight in them. Unhooked from outer contacts one finds the joy that is in the self. Whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here is happy.
chains.title: Pleasures with a beginning and an end

verses.m: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
verses.sa: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥

verses.m: The enjoyments born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they have a beginning and an end, Kaunteya. The wise do not delight in them.
verses.sa: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥

verses.m: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
verses.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥

chains.summary: Hope is the greatest sorrow and giving up hope is the greatest ease. Pingala slept in peace after she gave up her expectation. Whatever one calls mine becomes a source of pain when it is lost.
chains.title: The night she stopped waiting

verses.m: Whatever a person begins to think of as 'mine', that very thing becomes a source of anguish when it is lost.
verses.sa: किंचिदेव ममत्वेन यदा भवति कल्पितम् / तदेव परितापाय नाशे संपद्यते तदा

verses.m: Whatever pleasure desire brings in this world, and whatever great happiness there is in heaven, neither is worth a sixteenth part of the happiness that comes when craving ends.
verses.sa: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत्सुखम् / तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशीं कलाम्

chains.summary: Wherever there is craving, the round of the world is there. The list of things done and not done has never ended for anyone. Everyone suffers from straining, and no one sees it.
chains.title: Where craving is, the round is

verses.m: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
verses.sa: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥

gloss: Loosening the grip, the partner of practice in training the mind (6.35). Not indifference and not leaving one's duties.

hero.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
hero.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥

loci.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
loci.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥

loci.m: In pleasure lies the fear of disease; in high birth, the fear of a fall; in wealth, fear of the king; in honour, fear of humiliation; in strength, fear of enemies; in beauty, fear of old age; in learning, fear of rival debaters; in virtue, fear of the wicked; in the body, fear of death. Everything in this world carries fear; only dispassion is fearless.
loci.sa: भोगे रोगभयं कुले च्युतिभयं वित्ते नृपालाद्भयं माने दैन्यभयं बले रिपुभयं रूपे जराया भयम् । शास्त्रे वादिभयं गुणे खलभयं काये कृतान्ताद्भयं सर्वं वस्तु भयान्वितं भुवि नृणां वैराग्यमेवाभयम् ॥

practices.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
practices.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
practices.why: Shows loosening the pull of what the mind runs to.

practices.m: Thinking this over, I will not insist out of false affection. I bless you, son; only keep the bond of a mother, and don't forget me.
practices.sa: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥

practices.m: In a vessel full of awakening, filled with the oil of detachment and fitted with the wick of devotion, behold the lamp of knowing. In the hollow darkness of delusion it rises of itself. Make detachment the lower fire-stick and knowledge the upper.
practices.sa: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥
practices.why: Shows letting go as the fuel.

practices.m: So, Nidagha, knower of truth, in the dealings of worldly life, let go of whatever is lost, and take up whatever comes.
practices.sa: अतो निदाघ तत्त्वज्ञ व्यवहारेषु संसृतेः । नष्टं नष्टमुपेक्षस्व प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपाहर ॥
practices.why: Shows no second look at what has gone.

practices.sa: Your duty is to afford opportunities and to remove obstacles.

practices.m: Dhritarashtra: 'Everything is always unsettled, and this mind is always unsettled. Wise one, tell me of the state that is free from unrest.' Vidura: 'I see no peace for you apart from learning and discipline, apart from mastering the senses, apart from giving up greed.'
practices.sa: नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्रमिदं मनः / यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते नान्यत्र विद्यातपसो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् / नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्यामि तेऽनघ

practices.m: If you cannot do even this, then taking refuge in my yoga and with self restrained, give up the fruit of all actions.
practices.sa: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥
practices.why: Gives up the fruit of all actions.

practices.m: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
practices.sa: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥

stories.l: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
stories.s: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.

stories.l: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
stories.s: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
stories.t: Manki's song: desire, I know your root

stories.l: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
stories.s: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
stories.t: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting

stories.l: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.
stories.s: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
